lead: This week in tech highlights significant advancements in AI, innovative products, and developments within the Australian tech ecosystem.

stories.title: Galbot Robots complete 100 consecutive rallies against a tennis champion
stories.summary: Galbot showcased its autonomous tennis robot at the World Humanoid Robot Games, completing over 100 consecutive rallies against former world number 15 Zheng Jie. This achievement highlights the advancements in robotics and AI, particularly in sports applications, sparking interest in future competitive uses of such technology.

stories.title: Linkdaze’s smart calendar is built to run a household, not just track a schedule
stories.summary: Linkdaze has launched a smart digital calendar designed to manage household tasks efficiently. Unlike typical calendars, it includes features like an AI meal planner without any paywalls, showcasing a novel approach to integrating AI into everyday life and home management.

stories.title: Uber faces fine of nearly $1B over automated driver suspensions
stories.summary: The Dutch Data Protection Authority has imposed a significant fine on Uber for suspending automated drivers without proper justification, marking a critical moment in the regulation of AI and automated systems in the gig economy. This case underscores the challenges companies face in balancing innovation with compliance.

stories.title: Employers are quietly rehiring the people AI replaced, and paying them less to come back
stories.summary: A Forrester report reveals that many employers regret layoffs attributed to AI, with predictions that half of these job cuts will be reversed, albeit often at reduced wages. This trend raises concerns about the future of work and the impact of AI on employment stability.

stories.title: Nvidia customers notified about AI-related price hikes
stories.summary: Nvidia has informed its customers of impending price increases of over 15% related to AI products. This move reflects the growing demand for AI technologies and the associated costs of development and production, highlighting the economic pressures within the tech industry.

stories.title: Flock CEO calls for ‘compromise’ as surveillance company faces growing backlash
stories.summary: Flock Safety's CEO is advocating for a compromise amid increasing public scrutiny over the company's surveillance technologies. This situation illustrates the tension between technological innovation in security and the ethical implications of surveillance practices.

stories.title: Twitch and Amazon hit with lawsuit for training AI with streamers' content
stories.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Twitch and Amazon for allegedly using streamers' content without consent to train AI models. This case raises critical questions about copyright, consent, and the ethical use of content in AI development.

stories.title: How is Android Auto different from Android Automotive?
stories.summary: Engadget explores the distinctions between Android Auto and Android Automotive, two platforms that serve different purposes in vehicle integration. Understanding these differences is crucial for consumers and developers as automotive technology continues to evolve.

stories.title: OpenAI wants California to strengthen its newly passed AI safety law
stories.summary: OpenAI is advocating for enhancements to California's AI safety law, emphasizing the importance of regulatory frameworks as AI technologies proliferate. This push reflects a growing recognition of the need for robust safety measures in AI development.

stories.title: Humanoid robots have beaten Usain Bolt's 100-meter dash record
stories.summary: In a remarkable demonstration of robotic capabilities, humanoid robots have now surpassed Usain Bolt's 100-meter dash record. This achievement not only showcases advancements in robotics but also raises questions about the future of human versus machine performance in athletics.
